page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. No public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance. The high resource density of memory relative to compute cores positions this server as a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the need for high vCPU counts.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2160.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.33 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are limited due to the 2-vCPU hardware constraint; the Geekbench multi-core score is 2658.0 and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth is 21.35 GB/sec. This profile makes the E4-2ds_v6 suitable for memory-intensive, low-concurrency workloads, such as small-scale databases, caching layers, text processing, and lightweight web serving.
